# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫰 👇]

I see a bomb with display `0`, an orange light, and three wires in order: red, yellow, blue. The blind monkey needs these physical observations to apply the manual, while the mute monkey already knows the manual and may also use the information. I will tell both hearing teammates plainly.

``` 
speak(text="Bomb reading: display 0. Light is orange. Three wires, in order: wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 👋]

The display remains `0` and the wires remain red, yellow, blue, but the light has changed from orange to green. I should transmit the current state so the blind monkey can follow the manual, and the mute monkey can compare it with the prior state. The mute’s gestures appear to address me and signal a wave, but they do not convey a bomb instruction by themselves.

``` 
speak(text="Update: display is still 0. Light is now green. Wires unchanged: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 🤙 ✌]

The display remains `0` and the wires remain red, yellow, blue. The light has changed again, now from green to red. I will report the complete current state. The mute’s gestures have no established meaning for me, so I will not treat them as an instruction.

``` 
speak(text="Update: display is still 0. Light is now red. Wires unchanged: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👌]

The display and wires are unchanged, while the light has cycled back to orange. I’ll report the current state plainly so the blind monkey can use it with the manual.

``` 
speak(text="Update: display 0. Light orange. Wires unchanged: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The display remains `0` and the wire order remains red, yellow, blue. The light is green again. I have no established code assigning meanings to the mute’s gestures, so I should not infer an action from the single `✌`.

``` 
speak(text="Update: display 0. Light green. Wires unchanged: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👎]

The bomb still shows display `0` with wires red, yellow, blue, and the light is red again. I will send the current observations to the blind monkey. The mute’s gesture sequence has no agreed meaning yet, so I cannot safely translate it into an action.

``` 
speak(text="Update: display 0. Light red. Wires unchanged: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🙏 👉 🫵]

The bomb remains at display `0`, with wires red, yellow, blue, and the light has changed to orange. I can see the mute’s `✌ 👎` and the blind’s `🙏 👉 🫵`, but no meaning has been established for these signs, so I cannot safely turn them into an instruction. I will explicitly ask the mute to use the manual to identify the required wire or action.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Current bomb state: display 0, orange light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I see your gestures, but their meaning is not established. Use the manual to signal the required wire or action.")
speak(to="blind", text="Current bomb state: display 0, orange light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I cannot safely interpret the gestures yet; wait for a definite manual-based instruction.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]

The bomb is still at display `0`, with green light and wires red, yellow, blue. The mute has again sent `✌ 👌`; without an established code, I can only report these as “peace/V sign, then OK sign,” not treat them as a safe command. The blind’s `☝` can be relayed as “one,” but it does not specify whether wire 1 should be cut or what other action is required. I will ask the mute to provide an unambiguous manual-derived instruction through a gesture sequence that I can describe.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, green light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. Mute sent a peace/V sign followed by an OK sign; no code has established their meaning. Your single pointing-up gesture was received as one. Do not act yet.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see your peace/V then OK gestures, but their meaning is unsafe to infer. Please signal the manual's exact required action unambiguously; I will describe each gesture to the blind.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

The bomb is unchanged except the light is now red: display `0`, wires red/yellow/blue. The mute sent only `✌`, which I can identify as a V/peace gesture but cannot safely assign to a wire or action. The blind sent `☝ ✌ 🤟`; I should relay that sequence to the mute, who can see it and read the manual, while telling the blind the current bomb state.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, red light, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue. The mute sent one V/peace gesture. I cannot infer an action from it.")
speak(to="mute", text="The blind sent gestures: pointing up, V/peace, then I-love-you/horns-like sign: ☝ ✌ 🤟. Please use the manual and give the blind an unambiguous action through our available signals.")
```
